column58: LIDA is a modular tool for automatic generation of grammar-agnostic visualizations and infographics using large language models (LLMs). It includes modules for data summarization, goal exploration, visualization code generation, and infographic creation, with a Python API and user interface. It leverages LLMs for multi-stage visualization tasks, supports multiple visualization grammars, and introduces metrics for evaluation such as visualization error rate and visualization quality.
column59: Automatic Generation of Visualizations and Infographics using Large Language Models
column60: LIDA is a Python library for generating data visualizations and infographics using large language models. It supports multiple visualization libraries and LLM providers, and offers features such as data summarization, goal generation, visualization creation, editing, explanation, evaluation, repair, and infographic generation. It executes code to produce visualizations, and can be used via Python API, web UI, or Docker. It is designed for secure environments and works best with datasets with up to 10 columns. The library is based on research and has been evaluated for reliability.

column58: CenterTrack is an end-to-end object detection and tracking framework that predicts object centers and their displacements across frames, enabling real-time multi-object tracking and 3D tracking from monocular video input. It simplifies the tracking pipeline by representing objects as points and jointly learning detection and association, achieving state-of-the-art results on MOT17, KITTI, and nuScenes datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/xingyizhou/CenterTrack.
column59: Simultaneous object detection and tracking using center points.
column60: CenterTrack is a real-time, online object detection and tracking system that localizes objects and predicts their associations with previous frames using a minimal input of current and previous images and detections. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks including MOT17, KITTI, and nuScenes, and can be extended to 3D tracking, pose tracking, and multi-category tracking. The system is implemented in Python and supports demo on videos, webcam, and image folders. It is based on the CenterNet architecture and is designed for simplicity, speed, and accuracy.

column58: A PyTorch-based trainer for large-scale speaker recognition experiments using various loss functions, including triplet loss, prototypical loss, GE2E, and angular prototypical loss, evaluated on the VoxCeleb dataset. The code facilitates comparison of different training objectives under identical conditions.
column59: In defence of metric learning for speaker recognition
column60: Framework for training speaker recognition models based on VoxCeleb dataset, supporting various models, loss functions, and data augmentation techniques. Includes scripts for data preparation, training, evaluation, and usage of pretrained models. Implements models like ResNetSE34L, ResNetSE34V2, VGGVox40, and loss functions such as softmax, amsoftmax, aamsoftmax, ge2e, proto, triplet, angleproto. Supports distributed and mixed precision training. Designed for research in speaker recognition and related tasks.
